mechanisms.name: Vol-Control Deleveraging
mechanisms.summary: Vol-control and risk-parity funds size positions inversely to realized volatility. When realized vol jumps, their target leverage falls and they sell mechanically into weakness. The supply is price-insensitive and tends to cluster, which is why drawdowns can accelerate even when fundamentals have not changed.

signals_to_watch.field: compute 20d realized from FMP SPY quote returns vs VIX

mechanisms.feedback_loop: Higher realized vol forces vol-targeting funds to cut exposure, which adds selling pressure, which raises realized vol further. The loop only breaks when vol stops expanding and the trailing window starts to roll off elevated prints.

mechanisms.name: CTA Trend Reversal
mechanisms.summary: Managed-futures CTAs run momentum signals across equities, rates, FX, and commodities. When a trend reverses through their lookback window, they flip from long to short (or vice-versa) and the flip itself is large and fast. This is why sharp counter-trend moves often extend further than warranted.
trigger_conditions: S&P below its 50d and 100d MAs simultaneously
Sustained move >2 ATR against the prevailing 3m trend
mechanisms.feedback_loop: Once a trend signal flips, CTAs cover and reverse in size. The covering pushes price further through the breakeven, triggering more signals on shorter lookbacks, which compounds the move until positioning is flat or opposite.
fades_when: Price re-takes the broken trend line and holds for 5+ sessions
Realized vol compresses and trend re-establishes

mechanisms.name: Risk-Parity Unwind
mechanisms.summary: Risk-parity funds lever bonds to match equity risk and depend on negative stock-bond correlation for diversification. When stocks and bonds sell off together (typical in inflation shocks), the strategy bleeds on both legs and is forced to cut leverage across the whole book. This is mechanically different from vol-control because the trigger is correlation, not just vol.
trigger_conditions: Joint drawdown in SPY and TLT over 1m
T10Y2Y rapidly steepening on inflation prints

signals_to_watch.field: compute from FMP SPY and TLT daily returns

mechanisms.feedback_loop: Joint stock/bond losses raise the strategy's portfolio vol and break the diversification assumption. Funds cut leverage on both legs simultaneously, which deepens the joint sell-off, which keeps correlation positive and forces more cuts.

mechanisms.name: Gamma Squeeze
mechanisms.summary: When dealers are short calls (customers heavily long calls), they must buy the underlying as it rises to stay delta-hedged. That hedging buys into strength and accelerates the move higher. The squeeze ends when calls expire, are sold, or the rally exhausts and dealers re-flatten.
trigger_conditions: Heavy single-name call buying with rising open interest
Spot pinning above key strikes near OPEX

signals_to_watch.signal: Single-name short interest and call OI

mechanisms.feedback_loop: Customers buy calls, dealers hedge by buying spot, spot rises, dealer short-call delta grows, dealers buy more spot. The reflexive bid persists until call demand fades or expiration unwinds the position.
fades_when: Call open interest declines after OPEX
Heavy put buying restores positive dealer gamma

mechanisms.name: Long-Gamma Stabilization
mechanisms.summary: When dealers are net long gamma (customers short options), dealers sell into rallies and buy into dips to stay flat. That hedging supplies liquidity and compresses intraday range. Markets feel sticky and grinding because dealer flow is mean-reverting price.
trigger_conditions: Heavy index put-selling and overwriting flows
Spot pinning to large open-interest strikes
mechanisms.feedback_loop: Dealer long gamma forces them to fade moves, which compresses realized vol, which encourages more vol-selling by customers, which deepens dealer long gamma. Range stays narrow until a shock breaks the strikes the position is built around.
fades_when: Spot breaks decisively through dealer long-gamma strike cluster
Sharp put buying flips dealer gamma negative

mechanisms.name: Dealer Short-Gamma Chase
mechanisms.summary: When dealers are short gamma (customers long puts in a sell-off, or long calls in a rally), dealer hedging chases price in the direction of the move. This amplifies trends intraday and is a major source of fast tail moves into the close.
trigger_conditions: Heavy hedger put buying after a drawdown
Spot near a dense short-gamma strike cluster
mechanisms.feedback_loop: Dealer short gamma means hedges sell into weakness and buy into strength. The hedge flow amplifies the move, drawing more option demand, which deepens the dealer short and forces more chasing.
fades_when: OPEX rolls off the short-gamma exposure
Customers sell their puts/calls back to dealers
Spot moves clearly past the strike cluster

mechanisms.name: Repo Funding Stress
mechanisms.summary: Repo is the overnight plumbing where banks and hedge funds finance Treasury holdings. When SOFR jumps above the IORB or the Fed's RRP rate without a clear calendar reason, it signals collateral scarcity or balance-sheet strain at dealers. Stress here typically precedes risk-asset weakness because leveraged trades lose their funding leg.
trigger_conditions: SOFR > IORB by >5 bps for multiple days
mechanisms.feedback_loop: Higher repo rates raise the funding cost of leveraged trades, forcing some unwinds. Unwinds release collateral but also push spot prices around, which raises haircuts and hedging costs, tightening funding further until the Fed or dealers add reserves.
fades_when: Fed adds liquidity (standing repo, RRP drain)

mechanisms.name: TGA Drain/Refill Effect
mechanisms.summary: The Treasury General Account holds Treasury cash at the Fed. When the TGA falls, that cash flows into the banking system as reserves and tends to support risk assets. When it rises (post debt-ceiling refills, heavy issuance), reserves drain and conditions tighten. The effect is mechanical and on a fairly predictable issuance calendar.

signals_to_watch.field: WALCL minus RRP minus TGA proxy

mechanisms.feedback_loop: TGA drains add reserves to the system, easing conditions and supporting risk assets. TGA refills drain reserves into Treasury, tightening conditions; if RRP is already low, the drain comes from bank reserves directly and the impact is sharper.
fades_when: Fed adjusts RRP rate or balance-sheet runoff pace

mechanisms.name: RRP Unwind
mechanisms.summary: The Fed's reverse-repo facility absorbs excess money-market cash. When RRP balances fall, that cash typically rotates into T-bills and bank deposits, expanding usable liquidity in the system. A draining RRP buffers TGA refills and QT, but once RRP is empty, the same drains hit bank reserves directly.
trigger_conditions: Money-market funds rotating from RRP into bills
mechanisms.feedback_loop: Falling RRP releases cash into bills, which keeps short rates anchored and reserves stable, which supports risk-on conditions. The buffering effect ends abruptly when RRP nears zero and tightening pressure starts hitting reserves directly.
fades_when: Bill yields rise sharply above the RRP rate

mechanisms.name: Dollar Funding Stress
mechanisms.summary: Foreign banks and corporates borrow dollars synthetically via FX swaps. When the cross-currency basis widens (dollars expensive in swaps), it signals a global scramble for dollar funding. This typically coincides with risk-off, dollar strength, and stress in EM and credit.
mechanisms.feedback_loop: Dollar shortage pushes the dollar higher, which raises foreign borrowers' funding costs in local currency, which forces unwinds of dollar-denominated assets, which adds to the dollar bid. The loop breaks when central banks open swap lines or risk-off reverses.
fades_when: Fed opens or expands FX swap lines

mechanisms.name: Treasury Basis Trade Unwind
mechanisms.summary: Hedge funds run a massive levered trade short Treasury futures and long cash Treasuries to capture the basis. The trade depends on cheap repo funding. When repo tightens or rate vol spikes, the basis blows out, margin calls hit, and forced unwinds dump cash Treasuries — paradoxically pushing yields higher in a risk-off episode.
trigger_conditions: Repo rates spiking and CFTC leveraged short futures positioning extreme
mechanisms.feedback_loop: Basis blowout generates margin calls on the futures short. Funds raise cash by selling cash Treasuries, which pushes yields higher, which raises rate vol, which widens the basis further. The loop only breaks when the Fed adds liquidity or vol crushes.
fades_when: Fed standing repo facility usage spikes (relief)

mechanisms.name: HY Spread Widening Cascade
mechanisms.summary: High-yield credit is the canary for risk appetite. When HY OAS widens 50+ bps in a few weeks, equity drawdowns usually follow. The cascade comes from ETF redemptions forcing dealers to mark down inventory, which widens spreads further and prompts more redemptions.
trigger_conditions: HY OAS widens >75 bps in 4 weeks
HYG/JNK trading at persistent NAV discount
Energy or specific-sector blowouts dragging the index
mechanisms.feedback_loop: Spread widening triggers HY ETF redemptions, dealers mark down bonds, NAVs fall, more redemptions follow. Funding costs rise for low-quality issuers, which raises default risk, which widens spreads further.
fades_when: HY OAS rolls over for 5+ sessions

mechanisms.name: IG Spread Leadership
mechanisms.summary: Investment-grade spreads tend to lead equity drawdowns by 1-3 weeks because IG holders are more rate-sensitive and react earlier to financial-conditions shifts. When IG OAS widens while HY is still tight, it often signals top-down de-risking by real-money allocators before retail-driven HY moves.
trigger_conditions: IG OAS widens >15 bps in 2 weeks
mechanisms.feedback_loop: Real-money credit funds reduce IG exposure ahead of stress. Spreads widen, primary issuance slows, corporate buyback funding becomes more expensive, which weakens the equity bid and confirms the de-risking signal.

mechanisms.name: Credit-Equity Divergence
mechanisms.summary: When equities make new highs but credit spreads are widening (or vice-versa), one market is usually wrong and resolves toward the other. Credit tends to lead because credit investors focus on fundamentals and balance sheets while equity is more flow-driven near tops.
trigger_conditions: S&P new 6m high while HY OAS up >25 bps from 3m low
mechanisms.feedback_loop: Credit weakness raises the cost of capital and signals stress that equity has not priced. As credit deteriorates further, equity buybacks slow and de-risking accelerates, eventually pulling equity down to confirm the credit signal.
fades_when: HY OAS makes a new low

mechanisms.name: Passive Flow Dominance
mechanisms.summary: Passive funds buy index constituents on a market-cap basis regardless of valuation. As passive share grows, the largest names get the biggest inflows, breadth narrows, and price moves get less informative about fundamentals. The flip side is that any redemption hits the same names hardest.
mechanisms.feedback_loop: Passive inflows lift mega-caps, mega-cap outperformance attracts more passive (and momentum) flows, breadth narrows further, performance-chasing intensifies. The cycle inverts when redemptions hit and the same names lead the drawdown.

mechanisms.name: Systematic vs Discretionary Regime
mechanisms.summary: When systematic strategies (vol-targeting, CTAs, risk-parity) dominate marginal flow, markets trend smoothly and react mechanically to vol and price signals. When discretionary money is back in charge, narratives, earnings, and macro surprises matter more and intraday moves get noisier. Knowing which regime is active changes how to read the tape.
trigger_conditions: Tight intraday ranges with strong trends = systematic
VIX low with rising realized = mixed
mechanisms.feedback_loop: Systematic dominance compresses vol and steepens trends, which reinforces systematic flows. Eventually a discretionary catalyst (Fed, earnings, geopolitics) breaks the trend, vol spikes, systematic players cut, and discretionary money sets prices until the next compression.

mechanisms.name: Foreign Flow Rotation
mechanisms.summary: Foreign investors hold roughly a third of US Treasuries and a meaningful slice of US equities. When the dollar weakens or US real yields fall versus foreign alternatives, foreign flow can rotate out, pressuring USD assets. Conversely, dollar strength and yield premium attracts foreign capital and supports US risk assets.
trigger_conditions: TIC data showing net foreign selling
mechanisms.feedback_loop: Strong dollar plus high real yields attracts foreign flow into US assets, supporting equities and Treasuries and reinforcing dollar strength. When real yields compress or DXY rolls, the rotation reverses and US assets lose a structural bid.

mechanisms.name: ETF Creation/Redemption Arb
mechanisms.summary: Authorized participants arbitrage ETF prices against underlying baskets via creations and redemptions. In stress, the arb breaks down when underlying liquidity dries up (HY bonds, EM equities), and ETFs trade at large discounts to NAV. The discount itself can become a forced-sell signal that pressures the underlying further.

signals_to_watch.field: FMP quote HYG vs reported NAV
FMP quote EMB vs reported NAV

mechanisms.feedback_loop: Stress redemptions force APs to sell underlying bonds. Bond prices fall faster than ETF NAVs can update, ETFs trade at discount, more holders sell perceiving NAV deterioration, redemptions accelerate, more underlying selling.

mechanisms.name: COT Extreme Positioning
mechanisms.summary: When commercial hedgers are at multi-year extremes (e.g. heavily long after a sell-off, heavily short after a rally), it often marks a turning point because commercials trade on physical/fundamental knowledge. The flip side: leveraged-fund speculators at extremes are often wrong at turns and provide the fuel for reversals.
trigger_conditions: Open interest growing into the extreme
mechanisms.feedback_loop: Specs pile in chasing the trend; commercials hedge against them. As price approaches an extreme, specs are most exposed, commercials are most hedged. Any catalyst forces specs to cover, the cover becomes the next trend, and commercials gradually unwind their hedge.
fades_when: COT positioning normalizes back to z-score < 1
Open interest declines on the reversal

mechanisms.name: Put/Call Ratio Flips
mechanisms.summary: Equity put/call ratio extremes often precede short-term reversals. Extremely high P/C (panic put-buying) tends to mark capitulation lows; extremely low P/C (complacent call-buying) tends to mark distribution tops. The signal is sharpest when paired with VIX moves and breadth.
mechanisms.feedback_loop: Extreme put-buying pushes dealer gamma negative, increasing downside acceleration; once selling exhausts, the dealer hedge unwind becomes a buy and a sharp reversal follows. Mirror logic on extreme call-buying after rallies.
fades_when: Breadth confirms in the new direction

mechanisms.name: AAII Sentiment Extremes
mechanisms.summary: Retail sentiment surveys (AAII bull-bear, II) are slow but reliable contrarian indicators at multi-month extremes. When bears outnumber bulls by 20+ points after a drawdown, forward 3-6m returns skew positive. The reverse holds at frothy bullish extremes.
mechanisms.feedback_loop: Retail sells into drawdowns and buys into rallies, exhausting their own marginal buying or selling power. When the survey hits an extreme, the marginal flow has already happened and the next move tends to surprise the consensus position.

mechanisms.name: Fed Pivot Expectations
mechanisms.summary: Markets price expected Fed policy via the SOFR/Fed Funds curve. Sharp moves in pricing for cuts or hikes drive cross-asset flows: dovish repricing supports equities and gold and weakens the dollar; hawkish repricing does the reverse. The signal is most powerful when the market and the dot plot disagree.
trigger_conditions: Fed funds futures repricing >50 bps in a month
Powell speech or FOMC minutes catalysts
mechanisms.feedback_loop: Dovish repricing eases financial conditions (NFCI down, dollar down, equities up), which loosens conditions further and risks reigniting inflation, which can force a hawkish about-face. Each cycle whipsaws positioning.
fades_when: FOMC delivers and pricing converges to dots

mechanisms.name: Real-Yield Regime Shift
mechanisms.summary: Real yields are the discount rate for long-duration assets. When real yields rise sharply, growth stocks, gold, and crypto compress; when they fall, the same assets re-rate higher. Most equity factor rotations and the gold trade can be explained mostly by real-yield direction.
trigger_conditions: 10y real yield (T5YIFR proxy or TIPS) moves >50 bps in 1m
Gold/Nasdaq breaking trend on real-yield move
mechanisms.feedback_loop: Falling real yields lift duration-sensitive assets (tech, gold, crypto), supporting risk-on; rising real yields compress them and rotate flow into value/cyclicals. Each regime self-reinforces via factor flows until the rate environment changes.

mechanisms.name: Dollar Wrecking Ball
mechanisms.summary: When the dollar rallies sharply, it tightens global financial conditions: commodities priced in USD fall, EM borrowers struggle to service dollar debt, and US multinational earnings translate worse. A sustained DXY breakout reliably precedes risk-off in EM and commodities and weighs on US large-cap earnings.
trigger_conditions: DXY breaking above 200d MA with momentum
mechanisms.feedback_loop: Stronger dollar tightens global conditions, EM and commodities sell off, capital flows to US, dollar strengthens further. The loop only breaks when the Fed pivots or foreign central banks intervene meaningfully.

mechanisms.name: Inflation Expectations Re-Rate
mechanisms.summary: When breakevens and the 5y5y forward jump after CPI/PCE prints or supply shocks, the entire long end of the Treasury curve repriers. This re-rates discount rates across equities and triggers factor rotations from growth to value. Sustained de-anchoring forces a Fed reaction and amplifies the move.
mechanisms.feedback_loop: Higher breakevens raise nominal yields, which strengthens the dollar, which lowers commodity prices in USD, which can eventually anchor breakevens again. If breakevens de-anchor before that, the Fed must reset hawkish and the cycle resets harder.
fades_when: CPI prints in line for 2-3 months

mechanisms.name: Microstructure Liquidity Holes
mechanisms.summary: Top-of-book depth in S&P futures and major ETFs collapses during stress, sometimes by 80%+. With less liquidity, the same order size moves price more, which creates discontinuous gaps and amplifies the apparent severity of a sell-off. Holiday weeks and overnight sessions are especially vulnerable.
mechanisms.feedback_loop: Thin liquidity means the same flow moves price further. Larger price moves trigger stop-losses and systematic vol responses, adding flow into a market that cannot absorb it. The hole gets deeper until liquidity providers return at lower prices.

mechanisms.name: 0DTE Option Flow
mechanisms.summary: Zero-day-to-expiration options now drive a large share of intraday SPX flow. Because they have huge gamma near the strike, dealer hedging on 0DTE creates outsized intraday moves and pinning behavior. They can also magnify late-day reversals when the gamma profile flips.

signals_to_watch.field: options chain volume by expiry day

signals_to_watch.signal: Spot pinning to large OI strikes

mechanisms.feedback_loop: Dealer hedging on 0DTE positions buys/sells aggressively as spot crosses strikes. The hedging itself moves spot toward or through strikes, triggering more hedging. Effects flip at the close when the options expire and gamma resets.
fades_when: Open interest concentrates further out the curve

mechanisms.name: End-of-Month Rebalancing
mechanisms.summary: Pension and balanced funds rebalance monthly/quarterly back to target weights. When equities have rallied vs bonds, they sell stocks and buy bonds in the last 3 sessions of the month; the reverse in drawdowns. The flow is mechanical, sized in the tens of billions, and produces predictable end-of-month reversals.
trigger_conditions: S&P up >3% over month with bonds flat/down
Pension rebalancing estimates published by sell-side
mechanisms.feedback_loop: Cross-asset divergence triggers rebalance flow that fades the divergence. The flow itself is somewhat anticipated by traders who front-run it, which compresses the predictable portion but still leaves residual mean-reversion into the close.

mechanisms.name: Post-Earnings Drift
mechanisms.summary: Stocks tend to drift in the direction of an earnings surprise for 30-60 days afterward. Analysts revise estimates slowly, passive flows follow index rebalancing, and momentum traders extend the move. The effect is strongest when surprise + guidance are aligned and weakest when they diverge.
mechanisms.feedback_loop: Beat + raise prints attract momentum buyers, sell-side raises estimates, passive index flows follow on rebalances, and short-sellers cover. Each step extends the drift until the next print or a regime change.
fades_when: Stock breaks 50d MA against the drift

mechanisms.name: Guidance Compression Cycle
mechanisms.summary: When companies start cutting forward guidance, sell-side estimates follow with a lag, and stocks repeatedly miss the lowered bar before estimates fully reset. The cycle from peak guidance to estimate trough typically runs 2-4 quarters and is the single biggest driver of multi-quarter drawdowns in cyclicals.
trigger_conditions: Sector NTM EPS revisions negative for 3+ months
Margin trends rolling over in macro data
mechanisms.feedback_loop: Initial guidance cuts pressure stocks, which raises cost of capital, which forces more conservative guidance next quarter. Estimates lag the cuts, so prints keep missing, sell-side downgrades cascade, and the multiple compresses on top of the EPS cut.
fades_when: Cyclicals show first beats vs lowered bar

mechanisms.name: Margin Reset Cycle
mechanisms.summary: When input costs rise faster than companies can pass through (or vice-versa), gross margins compress (or expand) for several quarters before restabilizing. The reset is sticky because pricing power, contract structures, and labor agreements move slowly. Identifying which sectors are early/late in the cycle is a major source of relative-value alpha.
trigger_conditions: Sector gross margin trend changing direction for 2+ quarters
Wage growth or commodity costs decoupling from price index
mechanisms.feedback_loop: Cost pressure compresses margins, which forces price hikes, which dampens demand, which pressures volumes. Companies cut capex, supply shrinks, eventually pricing power returns and the margin cycle re-inflates. The full cycle typically runs 18-36 months.

mechanisms.name: Carry Trade Unwind
mechanisms.summary: Carry trades borrow in low-yield currencies (JPY, CHF) to fund higher-yielding assets (EM, credit, equities). They make small steady profits and then occasionally crash when funding currencies rally hard. The unwind is fast because the trade is heavily levered and the JPY/CHF moves trigger stops across the entire complex.
trigger_conditions: JPY rallying >2% in 3 sessions vs USD
Sharp drop in carry indices (e.g. EM FX vs USD)
mechanisms.feedback_loop: Funding currency rally triggers stops on carry trades, forced unwinds buy back the funding currency, which strengthens it further, triggering more stops. The unwind cascades through EM, HY credit, and equity vol until positioning is flat or central banks intervene.
